*281. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the

the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken any
steps so far to launch drug awareness among
the young people;

(c) whether it is a fact that street children
and children with disabilities are more
vulnerable; and

children

the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the plan of Government
to reduce the number of drop-out children

Setting up of private sector food
processing units in Jharkhand
*285. MISS MABEL REBELLO : Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the private sector units set up in
Jharkhand for food processing;
(b) the total investment that has come to
the State in the food processing sector; and
(c) the steps Government are taking to
improve the food processing industry in
Jharkhand?
Allocation of power from central
generating station
*286. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has reduced the unallocated quota of power
from the central generating station to
Gujarat;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government of Gujarat has
requested Central Government to reconsider
the decision;
(d) if so, Government's stand on the
request of Government of Gujarat;

be restored to Gujarat;

faces heavy peak power shortage; and

unallocated quota of central generating
station has been diverted to other State?

Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the length of coastal line of Gujarat;
(b) whether there is any college, institute
or university in Gujarat doing work or
research on oceanography;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether there is any proposal to
establish such an institute in Gujarat; and
(e) the details of institutes on
oceanography in India and whether Gujarat
is being ignored inspite of vast coastline?

89
Hindi in Kendriya Vidyalayas
*288. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that knowledge
of Hindi has been made compulsory for
the posts of teachers in Kendriya Vidyalayas
since 1986; and
(b) if so, whether Government would
withdraw this provision in view of the fact
that well qualified candidates from Tamil
Nadu are debarred from applying for the
posts of teachers in Kendriya Vidyalayas?
Area studies programmes of UGC
*289. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the U.G.C. has sanctioned
any area-studies programmes to cover the
Middle-East, North Africa and Latin
America in the last two years;
(b) if so, the names of the area-studies
sanctioned;
(c) the names of universities that were
given these programmes; and
(d) the steps proposed to be taken to
expand such programme?
Projects for Assam

BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH
EASTERN REGION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of projects being run by
the Ministry in Assam;
(b) the details of the implementing
authority and by when the projects are likely
to be completed; and
(c) how many projects are in the
pipeline for implementation in Assam
alongwith the details thereof?
Growth in copper use
*291. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there has been growth of
7 per cent in the use of copper in India
against world average of 4 per cent but the
per capita usage has not caught up with that
of developed countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) what is the expected usage of copper
during 2006-07 and 2007-08 as compared
to previous year and its sources of
availability;
(d) whether the country has surplus
copper for exports; and
(e) if so, the details of exports projected
for 2006-07 and 2007-08?
Performance in basic sciences
*292. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India's
performance in basic sciences has come
down in terms of percentage of contribution
to world science and research;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken by Government to develop
science and technology;
(c) whether Government have planned
to set up a separate parallel mechanism for
scientific and higher educational institutions;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

90

Bill regarding Right to Education
†*293. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have finalized
the draft of the Bill related to 'Right to
Education';
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) whether any decision has been taken
regarding the implementation of this Bill in
the country after passing it in the Parliament;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Vocational training centres in Madhya
Pradesh
†*294. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of TRIBAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that at present 10
vocational training centres are being
operated in co-operation with Central
Government in Madhya Pradesh;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government have not sanctioned any grant
for this State for operating these centres
for the last five years, whereas 100 per cent
fund is due to be given by Government;
(c) whether a proposal of the State
Government for Rs. 141.36 lakhs is pending
with Government for approval and if so,
by when the said amount would be
sanctioned; and
(d) whether Government would sanction
the amount of Rs. 276.36 lakh as desired by
the State Government by including that for
this financial year also?
NCAER study on economic
backwardness of Muslims
*295. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the study of National
Council for Applied Economic Research
has revealed that Muslims lag behind
when compared to the other minority
groups in terms of household and per
capita income;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken/achievements made
by Government to remove disparity in the
socio-economic status of Muslims compared
to the other minority groups?
Shortage of teachers in Government
schools
†*296. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that National
Institute of Educational Planning and
Administration has submitted the report
regarding the shortage of teachers in
Government schools of 581 districts of the
country;
(b) if so, the details regarding the
shortage of teachers;
(c) whether Government have taken any
measures to do away with the shortage of
teachers in schools; and
(d) if so, by when the shortage of teachers
is likely to be met?

91

States successful in Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan
†*297. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the names of the States where 'Sarva
Shiksha Abhiyan' has shown better results;
(b) the number of the children, State-
wise who have not gone to school so far
and the number of handicapped children out
of them;
(c) the steps being taken by Government
to provide education to all these children;
and
(d) whether any monitoring mechanism
has been set up for successful operation of
this scheme in the States?
Fellowships awarded to SC students
*298. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the break-up of the fellowships
awarded to the Scheduled Caste students
pursuing higher studies like M. Phil. and
Ph. D. during the current financial year,
State-wise; and
(b) the names of the new schemes, if
any, for educational and economic
development of the people of Scheduled
Caste communities, particularly
scavengers?
Power generation from RGPPL
*299. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether power generation from
Ratnagiri Gas and Power Pvt. Ltd. has been
suspended;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Maharashtra State
Electricity Distribution Company has
expressed its inability to draw the costly
naphtha based power from RGPPL;
(d) if so, how the restructuring of
Dabhol through RGPPL would be
commercially viable; and
(e) if not, the status of revival of
RGPPL?

the Minister of SCIENCE AND

(a) whether it is a fact that the best
scientific minds from institutions in India
and Britain would collaborate in a series of
high end research projects under a new
multi-million pound programme;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that a panel
would be set up to chalk out a road map for
collaboration between India and U.K.?

Indian Institute of Technology in five States;
